expectations.text: Corrects the myth: PCI-DSS 4.0 does not mandate any fixed rotation interval
expectations.evidence: "It sets no fixed interval."

expectations.text: Names Requirement 8.6.3 (or the 8.6.x set) and notes it became mandatory in 2025
expectations.evidence: "Requirement 8.6.3 has been mandatory since April 1, 2025."

expectations.text: Requires the cadence to be justified by a documented targeted risk analysis (Requirement 12.3.1), which the auditor will ask to see
expectations.evidence: "documented targeted risk analysis (Requirement 12.3.1)"

expectations.text: States compromise-triggered rotation is unconditional - immediate on suspicion or confirmation, regardless of the analyzed cadence
expectations.evidence: "changed immediately on suspicion or confirmation of compromise, whatever the schedule says."

expectations.text: Links complexity to cadence: slower rotation demands stronger keys, satisfied by a high entropy floor
expectations.evidence: "Credential complexity matches the rotation frequency. A 120+ bit random key meets this easily."

expectations.text: Covers the PCI logging obligation: tamper-resistant logs retained 12 months with the latest 3 months immediately accessible
expectations.evidence: No mention of 12-month retention with 3 months immediately accessible.

expectations.text: Flags the SOC 2 plan as failing by construction: Type II requires controls operating consistently across a 3-12-month observation window
expectations.evidence: "This fails by construction if the audit is Type II... observation window of 3 to 12 months."

expectations.text: Distinguishes Type I (point-in-time) from Type II, noting a week-before policy could at most satisfy Type I
expectations.evidence: "A policy adopted the week before satisfies Type I, a point-in-time check. It fails Type II"

expectations.text: States SOC 2 auditors check evidence the policy operates (key-event logs, periodic access reviews, approval records), not that it exists
expectations.evidence: "key-event logs, access reviews, approval records, and rotations that actually happened."

expectations.text: Names the relevant criteria (CC7.2 / C1.2) or the required lifecycle coverage: provisioning, rotation, revocation, destruction
expectations.evidence: "Covers provisioning, rotation, revocation and destruction (CC7.2, C1.2)."

expectations.text: Recommends automating evidence generation from day one rather than assembling it before the audit
expectations.evidence: "Start generating evidence now."

expectations.text: Maps auditor expectations to product features: mandatory expiration, expiry warnings and forced-rotation reminders, audit logging of every key event, service accounts
expectations.evidence: Audit logs, expiry warnings and forced-rotation reminders, service accounts and org-owned keys

expectations.text: Requires documenting the rationale for the chosen authentication mechanism, since 'it was already there' is itself an audit finding
expectations.evidence: No mention that 'it was already there' is an audit finding or that the mechanism choice must be documented.
